Negative Binomial Regression by IRLS and Newton-Raphson

Source: R/nbreg.R
nbreg.Rd

Fits a negative binomial (NB2) regression model for count data, with the estimation written from scratch: iteratively reweighted least squares (IRLS) for the regression coefficients, alternated with Newton-Raphson for the dispersion parameter theta. No general-purpose optimizer is used. The parameterization is the one used by MASS::glm.nb().

Usage

nbreg(
  formula,
  data,
  offset = NULL,
  control = nbreg_control(),
  weights = NULL,
  subset,
  na.action,
  model = TRUE,
  ...
)

Arguments

formula

A model formula such as y ~ x1 + x2. The response must contain non-negative whole numbers (counts). offset() terms are allowed.

data

A data frame (or list or environment) containing the variables in formula. If missing, variables are taken from the environment in which formula was created.

offset

Optional numeric vector added to the linear predictor, for example the log of an exposure time, with one value per row of data. It is added to any offset() terms in formula. NULL (the default) means no offset argument.

control

A list of settings from nbreg_control(). A plain list is also accepted and is checked by passing it to nbreg_control().

weights

Optional non-negative prior weights, one per observation. Each observation's contribution to the log-likelihood is multiplied by its weight, so a weight of 2 counts an observation twice and a weight of 0 leaves it out. Fractional weights are allowed.

subset

Optional expression selecting the rows of data to use.

na.action

How to handle missing values; defaults to getOption("na.action") (usually stats::na.omit()). stats::na.exclude() pads fitted values and residuals with NA to the original length.

model

Logical; if TRUE (the default), the model frame is kept in the result.

...

Not used. Supplying anything here is an error, so that a misspelled argument is not silently ignored.

Value

An object of class nbreg, a list containing:

coefficients

Named vector of estimated coefficients.

vcov

Variance-covariance matrix of the coefficients.

theta, SE.theta

The dispersion estimate and its standard error.

loglik

The maximized log-likelihood.

df

Number of estimated parameters (coefficients plus theta).

iter, converged

Number of outer passes, and whether the fit converged.

theta_bound

"none", or "upper"/"lower" if theta ended on a bound.

diverging

Names of coefficients flagged as diverging.

fitted.values, linear.predictors, residuals

Fitted means, linear predictors (including offsets), and response residuals.

prior.weights, offset, y, x

The weights, the combined offset, the (rounded) response and the model matrix.

nobs, df.residual

Number of observations with positive weight, and that number minus the number of coefficients.

loglik_trace

Log-likelihood after each outer pass.

terms, model, xlevels, contrasts, na.action

Model frame information used by the methods.

offset_arg_used

Whether the offset argument was supplied.

formula, call, control

The formula, the matched call and the settings used.

Details

The model is \(Y_i \sim NB(\mu_i, \theta)\) with \(\log \mu_i = x_i^\top \beta + o_i\), so that \(E(Y_i) = \mu_i\) and \(Var(Y_i) = \mu_i + \mu_i^2 / \theta\). A small \(\theta\) means much more spread than a Poisson model; as \(\theta \to \infty\) the model becomes Poisson.

The fit alternates two stages until the log-likelihood, the coefficients and \(\log\theta\) all stop changing (see nbreg_control()):

  1. IRLS for the coefficients, with theta held fixed. Each round computes the weights \(w_i = a_i \theta \mu_i / (\theta + \mu_i)\) and the working response \(z_i = (\eta_i - o_i) + (y_i - \mu_i)/\mu_i\) and solves a weighted least-squares problem.

  2. Newton-Raphson for theta, with the coefficients held fixed. Steps are taken on \(\log\theta\), using the slope and curvature of the log-likelihood (built from digamma() and trigamma()), with a line search that guarantees the log-likelihood increases.

Every step is checked: a step that would lower the log-likelihood, or lead to infinite or invalid values, is halved until it is acceptable. The log-likelihood itself is always evaluated exactly.

Starting values come from a Poisson IRLS fit and a moment-type estimate of theta. Standard errors of the coefficients come from \((X^\top W X)^{-1}\) at convergence, treating theta as known, as MASS::glm.nb() does; the standard error of theta comes from the curvature of the log-likelihood in theta.

Response values within 1e-8 of a whole number are accepted as rounding error and rounded before fitting.

Errors and warnings

Problems are signalled with classed conditions, so they can be caught selectively. Errors:

  • nbzinbreg_error_input: an invalid argument or invalid data. This covers a missing, non-formula, one-sided or two-part (|) formula; data that is not a data frame, list or environment, or has no rows; unused arguments in ...; an invalid model flag or control; variables that cannot be found; offset or weights of the wrong length; missing values with na.action = na.fail; no rows left after subset and na.action; a response that is not numeric, has more than one column, or contains negative, non-integer, missing or infinite values; weights that are not numeric, negative, infinite or all zero; an offset that is not numeric or not finite; a response that is zero for every observation; a model with no coefficients; covariates with infinite values; and too few observations for the number of coefficients.

  • nbzinbreg_error_rank: columns of the model matrix are linear combinations of other columns (the message names them).

  • nbzinbreg_error_fit: an unrecoverable numerical failure during fitting.

Warnings (the fit is still returned):

  • nbzinbreg_warning_convergence: an iteration or step-halving limit was reached; converged is then FALSE.

  • nbzinbreg_warning_theta: theta exceeds theta_warn (little or no overdispersion), or ended on one of its bounds.

  • nbzinbreg_warning_divergence: some coefficients run off toward plus or minus infinity, typically because a group has only zero counts. Their estimates, standard errors and p-values are not meaningful.

  • nbzinbreg_warning_se: standard errors could not be computed.

See also

nbreg_control(), zinbreg(), nbreg-methods

Examples

# The 8-observation example used in the package's design notes
d <- data.frame(x = 1:8, y = c(1, 0, 6, 1, 9, 2, 20, 4))
fit <- nbreg(y ~ x, data = d)
fit
#> 
#> Call:
#> nbreg(formula = y ~ x, data = d)
#> 
#> Negative binomial regression (NB2, log link)
#> 
#> Coefficients:
#> (Intercept)            x  
#>     -0.1133       0.3440  
#> 
#> Theta: 1.509 (SE 1.025)
#> Log-likelihood: -20.3448 on 3 df;  AIC: 46.6896
#> Observations: 8
summary(fit)
#> 
#> Call:
#> nbreg(formula = y ~ x, data = d)
#> 
#> Pearson residuals:
#>     Min      1Q  Median      3Q     Max 
#> -0.9033 -0.8066 -0.4540  0.9408  1.3534 
#> 
#> Coefficients:
#>             Estimate Std. Error z value Pr(>|z|)  
#> (Intercept)  -0.1133     0.8416  -0.135    0.893  
#> x             0.3440     0.1545   2.226    0.026 *
#> ---
#> Signif. codes:  0 '***' 0.001 '**' 0.01 '*' 0.05 '.' 0.1 ' ' 1
#> 
#> Theta: 1.509 (SE 1.025)
#> Log-likelihood: -20.3448 on 3 df
#> AIC: 46.6896;  BIC: 46.9279
#> Observations: 8;  residual df: 6
#> Outer passes: 4;  converged: yes

# Article counts of biochemistry PhD students
if (requireNamespace("pscl", quietly = TRUE)) {
  data("bioChemists", package = "pscl")
  fit2 <- nbreg(art ~ fem + mar + kid5 + phd + ment, data = bioChemists)
  summary(fit2)
}
